newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Bank Melbourne, Westpac to join Victoria units.
newsitem.headline: Bank Melbourne, Westpac to join Victoria units.

text.p: Bank of Melbourne Ltd and Westpac Banking Corp said on Thursday they had agreed to to combine their retail operations in Victoria and carry on under the name Bank of Melbourne with local management as part of their A$1.435 billion merger plan.
Bank of Melbourne Chairman Christopher Stewart said in a statement that the combined retail network would give a much better coverage of the Victorian market than either bank had had previously.
He added that many Bank of Melbourne customers dealt with other banks for services which Bank of Melbourne did not currently provide, such as credit cards, funds management products and leasing.
"The merger will make all of these and other products avaliable at all Bank of Melbourne branches," Stewart added.

In a separate statement Westpac's Managing Director Robert Joss said: "Our regional banking approach will ensure Bank of Melbourne becomes a stronger competitive force in Victoria and retains its local indentity."

"This approach which was established in Western Australia and New Zealand will provide the framework for Victoria in delivering local product and marketing discretion, local credit decision making with Westpac's overall credit policy guidelines, local personnel management and local community sponsorship," Joss said.

The Bank of Melbourne brand will be used throughout Victoria for the combined retail, small business and commercial operations, while Westpac's brand name in the corporate and institutional markets will continue in the non-retail market using the formula applied in Western Australia.

The offer for 100 percent of the share capital of Bank of Melbourne is subject to approvals from the Federal Treasurer, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission, Reserve Bank of Australia and Bank of Melbourne's ordinary shareholders.
